Save and load parameters as GGUF

Source: R/persist.R
zl_save.Rd

zl_save() writes every parameter of a store, and optional metadata, to a GGUF file, the format of the 'ggml' library, which other tools (llama.cpp, the 'gguf' Python package) read. zl_load() reads one into a new store, with every tensor in single precision unless keep_types is TRUE.

Usage

zl_save(p, path, type = c("f32", "f16", "bf16"), metadata = list())

zl_load(path, keep_types = FALSE)

Arguments

p

A parameter store.

path

The file to write or read.

type

The type tensors are written as: "f32", "f16" or "bf16". Half-precision types halve the file and round each value.

metadata

A named list of key-value pairs to store with the tensors: each value a character, integer, double or logical vector without NA. Keys starting with zulm. are reserved.

keep_types

For zl_load(): FALSE widens every tensor to f32; TRUE keeps f16 and bf16 tensors in their type in memory (see zl_params() for the cost in precision).

Value

zl_save() returns path invisibly. zl_load() returns a parameter store whose "metadata" attribute is the file's metadata as a named list.

Details

Only parameters are saved: the state of an optimiser is not, so training resumed from a loaded store starts with fresh optimiser state.

Tensor dimensions follow R's order: a GGUF tensor of ne = {d1, d2} is an R matrix of dim = c(d1, d2), which NumPy reads as an array of shape (d2, d1) holding the same bytes.

Examples

p <- zl_params()
zl_param(p, "w", c(3, 2))
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".gguf")
zl_save(p, path, metadata = list(model = "example", width = 3L))
q <- zl_load(path)
all.equal(zl_param_get(q, "w"), zl_param_get(p, "w"))
#> [1] TRUE
attr(q, "metadata")$model
#> [1] "example"
unlink(path)
